en: The Sūtra on the Virtues of an Arhat Spoken by the Buddha,
translated by the Tripitaka Master of the Western Heaven, Imperial Censor of the Third Order, Acting Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments,
Great Master of Enlightened Teaching, Subject Faxian, by imperial decree.
At that time, the World-Honored One was seated upon a prepared seat within the Anāthapiṇḍada Monastery in Śrāvastī.

Various bhikṣus, as well as devas, nāgas, and the eight classes of beings—both human and non-human—surrounded the World-Honored One, silently joining their palms to listen to what the Buddha would say.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the bhikṣus:
"I now praise all the great śrāvakas, who are able to practice the Buddha-dharma with purity and have fully realized their own virtues within their respective fruits."
"Listen attentively, all of you, and reflect well upon it; I shall explain it to you in due order.

'O Bhikṣus! Among my disciples there is a Great Śrāvaka who, having renounced his royal throne and long practiced the life of a renunciant, was the first to realize the Path and is foremost in the holy life (brahmacarya); he is the Bhikṣu Kauṇḍinya.'"
"Furthermore, there is a śrāvaka who has little greed and always delights in practicing the dhūta austerities; he is the bhikṣu Mahākāśyapa.
Furthermore, there is a śrāvaka endowed with great eloquence and foremost in wisdom; he is the bhikṣu Śāriputra."
"Furthermore, there is a śrāvaka who practices with diligence and possesses great supernormal powers; he is the bhikṣu Maudgalyāyana.
Furthermore, there is a śrāvaka who, upon looking out, attains the great divine eye; he is the bhikṣu Aniruddha."
"Furthermore, there is a śrāvaka who is endowed with meditative concentration and wisdom and is foremost in extensive learning; he is the bhikṣu Ānanda.
Furthermore, there is a śrāvaka who is well-versed in ritual protocols and is able to uphold the Vinaya Piṭaka; he is the bhikṣu Upāli."
“Furthermore, there is a śrāvaka who is able to preach the sublime Dharma amidst the great assembly; he is the bhikṣu Pūrṇa Maitrāyaṇīputra.
Furthermore, there is a śrāvaka who is fully provided with all necessities such as seats and bedding; he is the bhikṣu Naladaputra.”
"Furthermore, there is a śrāvaka whose voice in preaching the Dharma is like the roar of a lion; this is the bhikṣu Piṇḍolabhāradvāja.
Furthermore, there is a śrāvaka who is well-versed in the Sūtras and Vinaya and is able to discourse on their meaning; this is the bhikṣu Kātyāyana."
"Furthermore, there is a śrāvaka who possesses the foremost faith and understanding in the Buddha's teachings; he is the bhikṣu Makarika.
Furthermore, there is a śrāvaka who, through his cultivation and attainment of the fruits [of the path], brings glory to his clan; he is the bhikṣu Kālodāyin."
“Furthermore, there is a śrāvaka who possesses a great and wondrous voice in his preaching; he is the bhikṣu Vādirāta.
Furthermore, there is a śrāvaka who is skilled in elegant speech and capable of discourse; he is the bhikṣu Kumāra-Kāśyapa.”
"Furthermore, there is a śrāvaka who possesses great diligence throughout the four modes of conduct; he is the bhikṣu Surūpaguptavatsa.
Furthermore, there is a śrāvaka who is able to possess swift supernatural powers in all places; he is the bhikṣu Vārhika."
"Furthermore, there is a śrāvaka who is well able to advance toward awakening and attain the fruit; he is the bhikṣu Cilliyaka.
Furthermore, there is a śrāvaka who is able to possess the supernormal power of the fire element; he is the bhikṣu Sugata."
“Furthermore, there is a śrāvaka who abandoned a noble clan to delight in going forth; he is the bhikṣu Bhadrika.
Furthermore, there is a śrāvaka who abandoned his status as a member of the Śākya royal clan to go forth; he is the bhikṣu Uruvilvā-Kāśyapa.”
"Furthermore, there is a śrāvaka who first accepted an invitation at a stupa site; he is the bhikṣu Pūrṇa.
Furthermore, there is a śrāvaka who possesses great wisdom in accordance with whatever he expounds; he is the bhikṣu Kauṇḍinya."
"Furthermore, there is a śrāvaka whose deportment is upright and disciplined and whose physical appearance is perfect; he is the bhikṣu Upasena Maṅkhaliputra.
Furthermore, there is a śrāvaka who is foremost in understanding the meaning of the Buddha’s teachings; he is the bhikṣu Puṇṇa Mantāniputta."
"Furthermore, there is a śrāvaka who is able to sever doubts regarding the principle of the Four Truths; he is the bhikṣu Mahāpāṭaka.
Furthermore, there is a śrāvaka whose speech is straightforward and without concealment, who admonishes the bhikṣus; he is the bhikṣu Kapphiṇa."
"Furthermore, there is a śrāvaka who constantly exhorts and admonishes the bhikṣuṇīs; this is the bhikṣu Nāṭaka.
Furthermore, there is a śrāvaka whom many people look up to and from whom they constantly receive material offerings; this is the bhikṣu Sivara."
“Furthermore, there is a śrāvaka whose faculties are so concealed that no one can fathom them; this is the bhikṣu Nanda.
Furthermore, there is a śrāvaka who maintains the precepts and the Vinaya with such purity and flawlessness; this is the bhikṣu Rāhula.”
"Furthermore, there is a śrāvaka who experiences little illness and little affliction in his received body; this is the bhikṣu Muktika.
Furthermore, there is a śrāvaka who constantly practices giving and is able to remain undiminished while being foremost in the realization of emptiness; this is the bhikṣu Subhūti."
"Furthermore, there is a śrāvaka who is able to speak sparingly at all times; he is the bhikṣu Aṅgajitīya.

Furthermore, there is a śrāvaka who is fully endowed with the knowledge of past lives (pūrvanivāsajñāna), having attained the ability to explain all manner of events from his former existences; he is the bhikṣu Subhūti."
“Furthermore, there is a śrāvaka who is able to cultivate pure conduct and dwells well in mountain crags; this is the bhikṣu Rāṣṭrapāla.
Furthermore, there is a śrāvaka for whom bedding, seating, and all other requisites are fully provided; this is the bhikṣu Gavāmpati.”
"Furthermore, there is a śrāvaka who is able to attain meditative concentration while advancing [on the path]; that is the bhikṣu Revata.
Furthermore, there is a śrāvaka who practices so as to sever afflictions already arisen; that is the bhikṣu Nārada."
“Furthermore, there is a śrāvaka who is able to suppress unarisen afflictions; he is the bhikṣu Mṛgīputra.
Furthermore, there is a śrāvaka who constantly possesses compassionate conduct; he is the bhikṣu Revata.”
"Furthermore, there is a śrāvaka who is able to practice compassion skillfully amidst suffering; this is the bhikṣu Pindola-Bharadvāja.
Furthermore, there is a śrāvaka who possesses the great practice of equanimity; this is the bhikṣu Vanavāsin."
"Furthermore, there is a śrāvaka who possesses great power of equanimity; he is the bhikṣu Jeta.
Furthermore, there is a śrāvaka who is fully able to comprehend both wholesome and unwholesome dharmas; he is the bhikṣu Kāṇakavatsa."
"Furthermore, there is a śrāvaka who is able to swiftly sever all worldly desire; that is the bhikṣu Nanda.
Furthermore, there is a śrāvaka who is able to swiftly eliminate all anger; that is the bhikṣu Māṭhara."
"Furthermore, there is a śrāvaka who is able to cultivate the supreme fruit and swiftly sever conceit; he is the bhikṣu Mana-vā.
Furthermore, there is a śrāvaka who is able to swiftly sever the dharmas of delusion; he is the bhikṣu Varado-ja-mana-vā."
"Furthermore, there is a śrāvaka who practices with purity and has a thorough understanding of cause and effect; he is the bhikṣu Mañjuśrī.
Furthermore, there is a śrāvaka who is able to cultivate the fruits of sainthood and possesses great, sharp faculties; he is the bhikṣu Aṅgulimāla."
"Furthermore, there is a śrāvaka whose three karmas are well-disciplined and whose faculties are supple; he is the bhikṣu Sariputra.
Furthermore, there is a śrāvaka who is well able to inquire about subtle and profound meanings; he is the bhikṣu Mahāki."
"Furthermore, there is a śrāvaka who possesses great eloquence in discourse; that is the bhikṣu Rādha.
Furthermore, there is a śrāvaka who is able to question his mother regarding the most profound meaning; that is the bhikṣu Kālapa."
"Furthermore, there is a śrāvaka who is well-versed in the Dharma and its meaning and compiles verses;
he is the bhikṣu Vāgīśa. Furthermore, there is a śrāvaka whose every utterance is entirely true; he is the bhikṣu Viśākha-Pañcaśikha."
"Furthermore, there is a śrāvaka who, with a pure mind, always delights in seeking the Dharma; he is the bhikṣu Darimiga.
Furthermore, there is a śrāvaka who practices the conduct of joy and possesses the power of patience; he is the bhikṣu Pūraṇa."
"Furthermore, there is a śrāvaka who internally contemplates the Dharma and has thoroughly realized his own fundamental mind; he is the bhikṣu Yaśas.
Furthermore, there is a śrāvaka who is skilled in interpreting signs and omens within worldly matters; he is the bhikṣu Mṛgāśiras."
“Furthermore, there is a śrāvaka who, with a distinguished mind, skillfully understands the sublime Dharma; this is the bhikṣu Dharmaka.
Furthermore, there is a śrāvaka who has mastery over desire and thoroughly comprehends the past and future; this is the bhikṣu Pudgala.”
"Furthermore, there is a śrāvaka who is able to speak skillfully at all times; he is the bhikṣu Pāmanā.
Furthermore, there is a śrāvaka who is skillful in means and can expound the sublime Dharma; he is the bhikṣu Darimira."
"Furthermore, there is a śrāvaka who has attained the meaning of the sublime Dharma and is able to explain it in successive order; he is the bhikṣu Gavāṃpati.
Furthermore, there is a śrāvaka who preaches the Dharma at all times without weariness; he is the bhikṣu Kapphiṇa."
"Furthermore, there is a śrāvaka who always maintains a solemn and dignified demeanor and constantly harbors joy; he is the bhikṣu Anabhibhūta.
Furthermore, there is a śrāvaka who is always endowed with abundant joy; he is the bhikṣu Saṃbuddha."
"Furthermore, there are śrāvakas who attain liberation through wisdom alone; the bhikṣu Sujāta is such a one.
Furthermore, there are śrāvakas who are able to attain liberation through both concentration and wisdom; the bhikṣu Vatsa is such a one."
"Furthermore, there is a śrāvaka who is able to sever greed; he is the bhikṣu Cañcamuka.
Furthermore, there is a śrāvaka endowed with excellent liberation; he is the bhikṣu Vairāṭasimha."
“Furthermore, there is a śrāvaka who has purified his practice and possesses knowledge, faith, and understanding; he is the bhikṣu Cāṅga.
Furthermore, there is a śrāvaka who has attained the most preeminent excellence in the world; he is the bhikṣu Mahika.”
"Furthermore, there is a śrāvaka whose wisdom and understanding are lofty and profound, capable of refuting the doctrines of outsiders; he is the bhikṣu Most Victorious (Jinavara).
Furthermore, there is a śrāvaka who is endowed with right view and well able to defeat the armies of Māra; he is the bhikṣu Nigrodhamiśra."
“Furthermore, there is a śrāvaka who is able to skillfully dispel ignorance and delusion through wisdom; he is the bhikṣu Yaśas Kāśyapa.
Furthermore, there is a śrāvaka who constantly practices equanimity; he is the bhikṣu Vakkula.”
"Furthermore, there is a śrāvaka who cultivates pure wisdom and gradually diminishes his defilements; he is the bhikṣu Śūraṇakoṭīkarṇa.
Furthermore, there is a śrāvaka who possesses great purity in his progress toward enlightenment; he is the bhikṣu Udāru."
"Furthermore, there is a śrāvaka whose physical form is flawless and whose faculties are complete; he is the bhikṣu Aṅgīrasa.
Furthermore, there is a śrāvaka who is well-versed in the practice of the Dharma of emptiness; he is the bhikṣu Devala."
"Furthermore, there is a śrāvaka who has developed profound faith and understanding regarding the dharma of emptiness; he is the bhikṣu Cunda.
Furthermore, there is a śrāvaka who possesses only supernatural powers within his own fruit; he is the bhikṣu Mahākāśyapa."
"Furthermore, there is a śrāvaka who is well able to contemplate the meaning of the eight liberations; this is the bhikṣu Śraddhādhimukta.
Furthermore, there is a śrāvaka who delights in exquisite robes within his deportment; this is the bhikṣu Maudgalyāyana."
“Furthermore, there is a śrāvaka who extensively expounds the sublime principles and possesses a great retinue; he is the bhikṣu Sañjayin.
Furthermore, there is a śrāvaka who is fully endowed with meditative concentration and wisdom and constantly receives offerings from gods and humans; he is the bhikṣu Subhūti.”
"Furthermore, there is a śrāvaka who has resolved to leave the household life and delights in practicing the noble conduct;
this is the bhikṣu Viśāla. Furthermore, there is a śrāvaka who left the household life because he encountered adverse circumstances; this is the bhikṣu Mūḍha-Citrabhānu."
"Furthermore, there is a śrāvaka who, weary of saṃsāra, seeks to go forth [into homelessness]; he is the bhikṣu Sunārikadevīka.
Furthermore, there is a śrāvaka who, having realized the world is unstable, has developed deep weariness toward it; he is the bhikṣu Sunārikaparājita."
"Furthermore, there is a śrāvaka who remains silent and composed, his demeanor upright and disciplined; he is the bhikṣu Sahiṣṇuka.
Furthermore, there is a śrāvaka who practices with purity, whose nature is simple and who possesses little eloquence; he is the bhikṣu Upendana."
"Furthermore, there is a śrāvaka who constantly practices alone and is endowed with tranquil conduct; this is the bhikṣu Nandika.
Furthermore, there is a śrāvaka who is skilled in concentration and wisdom and has attained great liberation; this is the bhikṣu Kambala."
"Furthermore, there is a śrāvaka who is able to purify those who are deluded; he is the bhikṣu Nāgita.
Furthermore, there is a śrāvaka who was the last to renounce the world while practicing pure conduct; he is the bhikṣu Subhadra."
At that time, the World-Honored One further spoke in verse:
"The holy life with little desire, Wisdom and supernormal powers,
The divine eye and great learning, And purity in upholding the Vinaya."
Sitting and reclining in peace and ease, possessing the voice of the lion’s roar,
endowed with faith, understanding, and profundity, skillfully discerning the Sūtras and Vinaya,
bringing glory to his clan, and possessing a great, subtle, and wondrous sound.
The power of his diligence is inconceivable; he is skillful in discourse and possesses great, swift supernormal powers.
Having first accepted the invitation at the sacred stupa, he speaks directly without concealment, admonishing the bhikṣus and bhikṣuṇīs.
Able to keep the sense faculties concealed, constantly upholding the pure precepts,
having little illness or affliction in the body, always practicing generosity,
speaking little and remaining mostly silent, and being endowed with the knowledge of past lives.
With abundant bedding and seating, always delighting in dwelling among mountain crags;
having severed afflictions already arisen, causing those not yet arisen to cease;
constantly entering samādhi, with great compassion and the intent to benefit others.
All faults can be eliminated; with a compassionate heart, one stills the wheel of suffering.
Constantly practicing both wholesome and unwholesome dharmas, one swiftly removes the marks of self-conceit (*asmimāna*).
Able to sever greed, hatred, and delusion, the faculties become sharp and pure.
Well-versed in the law of cause and effect, Able to inquire into the most profound principles,
With all faculties made supple, And endowed with great eloquence,
He questioned his mother on the profound meaning, Capable of proclaiming words of truth.
He skillfully compiles verses; his power of patience is firm;
he always delights in the most profound Dharma; endowed with the power of patience, he thoroughly understands the fundamental mind and is able to discern all signs and characteristics.
Possessing patience and joy, they always have mastery over their desires;
having entered deeply into the wondrous Dharma-gate, they skillfully resolve the mind with wisdom.
They extensively proclaim the subtle and wondrous Dharma, teaching the Dharma according to its proper sequence.
Teaching extensively without weariness, with joy and great gladness,
they have realized liberation through wisdom and attained liberation through both concentration and wisdom;
with craving forever eliminated, they have deeply entered the gateway of liberation.
Having realized and gained confidence in understanding, he has attained supremacy in the world;
able to defeat external teachers, he skillfully awakens the ignorant and deluded;
able to shatter the armies of all Māras, he leaves the household life to abandon suffering and affliction.
With pure wisdom and few defilements, Perfectly endowed with all faculties,
Understanding emptiness and the non-dual dharma, Possessing the attainment of supernormal powers,
Skillfully contemplating the eight liberations, And delighting in robes of exquisite color.
Having a great circle of kinsmen, receiving offerings from humans and devas,
he left the home life out of faith; constantly practicing impartial conduct,
he grew weary of worldly pleasures and left the home life, deeply loathing the suffering of saṃsāra.
Constantly practicing a tranquil mind, possessing a modicum of eloquence,
abiding in silent stillness, and deeply capable in the practice of liberation—
purifying those who are deluded and ignorant— one who possesses such virtues as these.
"Therefore, he is called an Arhat.
At that time, having spoken these verses, the World-Honored One further addressed the bhikṣus, saying:
"Within this assembly there are ten great śrāvakas; I shall now proclaim their names, which you should listen to well."

"These are the so-called bhikṣu Kauṇḍinya, the bhikṣu Kātyāyana, the bhikṣu Pūrṇa, the bhikṣu Bakula, the bhikṣu Revata, the bhikṣu Aṅgirimāra, the bhikṣu Yaśas, the bhikṣu Sujāta, the bhikṣu Koṭīkarṇa, and the bhikṣu Vaiśāla—these ten great śrāvakas serve as the leaders within this assembly."
At that time, the Blessed One again addressed the bhikṣus, saying:
"I now praise the great śrāvaka bhikṣuṇīs, who likewise cultivate their own virtues within their respective fruits."

Among my bhikṣuṇīs, there is a great śrāvaka bhikṣuṇī who abandoned her royal lineage long ago to go forth, whose conduct is pure, and who constantly cultivates the holy life; she is the bhikṣuṇī Mahāprajāpatī.
"The bhikṣuṇī Pāṭaccarā is the one who has few desires, is content, and practices the dhūta austerities.
The bhikṣuṇī Lakṣaṇā is the one whose wisdom is profound and vast, and who possesses great eloquence."
“The bhikṣuṇī Padmavarṇā is one whose virtuous conduct and majestic power are unsurpassed.
The bhikṣuṇī Sumā is one who has attained the divine eye through her diligent practice.”
“The bhikṣuṇī Śubhakarmarā has cultivated the wisdom of hearing and reflection and attained great erudition.
The bhikṣuṇī Kṛśā is one who is well-versed in the Vinaya and whose conduct as a preceptor is without flaw.”
"The one who is skillful in eloquently expounding the sublime Dharma is the Bhikṣuṇī Dharmadinnā.
The one who constantly proclaims the sublime Dharma with a mind of loving-kindness is the Bhikṣuṇī Dharmā, daughter of the Śākyas."
“The bhikṣuṇī Mahāśvetā is she who has diligently cultivated the noble causes and brought glory to her clan.
The bhikṣuṇī, mother of the householder Śikhara, is she who sought the great fruit with resolve and left the household life out of faith.”
“The bhikṣuṇī Yaśodharā, mother of Rāhula, is she who planted excellent roots in past lives and possesses great merit and virtue.
The bhikṣuṇī Śaṅkhinī is she who has always aspired to practice and possesses great diligence.”
"She who is capable of swiftly attaining her own fruit is the Bhikṣuṇī Bhadrā.
She whose wisdom is profound and who is well-versed in the Sūtras and Vinaya is the Bhikṣuṇī Citrā."
"In this way, these bhikṣuṇīs shall serve as leaders within the great assembly.
At that time, the World-Honored One again addressed the bhikṣus, saying:
"Listen attentively!
I shall now praise the upāsakas, who, within their hearts of faith, also cultivate their own practice.
These are those such as the upāsaka Poṣadha and the upāsaka Bāli, who first gave rise to faith and took refuge in the Triple Gem, and who dwell in Uruvilvā.
One who is fully endowed with the ability to practice the pure dharma of the precepts is the upāsaka Nakula’s father; he dwells at Vāṇija.
One who constantly practices giving to the Saṃgha is the Elder Anāthapiṇḍada; he dwells in Śrāvastī.
The Elder Śubhavyūha, who cultivated noble causes in the past and possessed great merit, resided in the city of Śrāvastī.
The Elder Agrasena, who constantly provided food and drink to the community of monks, resided in the city of Vaiśālī.
The Elder who is constantly able to practice various forms of giving within the Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha is the one who dwells in Rājagṛha.
The Elder Mahānāman, who constantly bestows medicinal decoctions upon those suffering from illness, dwells in Kapilavastu.
Those who are able to constantly practice acts of compassion within a state of faith are the elder Mṛgāra, who dwells in the city of Mahāśālā;
the elder Śreṣṭhika, who skillfully transforms the assemblies through the four means of attraction (saṃgrahavastu); and Aṭavaka, who dwells together with him in Mahāraṇya.
From the initial arousal of the mind of faith, one is able to possess great wisdom: the Elder Upāli is he who dwells in the city of Nālandā.
One is able to deliver the lion’s roar in discourse amidst the great assembly: the Elder Śūra is he who dwells in the city of Rājagṛha.
The Elder Nalimukha-Ṛṣi, who possesses great wisdom capable of refuting non-Buddhist teachers, dwells in the city of Vaiśālī.
He constantly expounds the subtle and wondrous Dharma within the great assemblies. The Elder Citra dwells in the city of Supratiṣṭhita.
One who possesses great eloquence in all discussions is King Prasenajit; he resides in the city of Śrāvastī.
One who is foremost among those of sharp faculties within the community of the faithful is the younger brother of King Gālava; he dwells in the city of Śrāvastī.
One who possesses great wisdom within a mind of faith is the upāsaka Śrona; he dwells in Śrāvastī.
One who maintains the holy life (brahmacarya) within a mind of faith is the upāsaka Bhāradvāja; he dwells in Śrāvastī.
Possessing precious treasures and abundant storehouses, widely gathering people and foremost in extensive learning—this was King Bimbisāra of Magadha, whose capital was the city of Rājagṛha.
He constantly arouses the bodhicitta toward the Triple Gem and has many sons in this world; the elder Jīvaka is one such person, residing in the city of Rājagṛha.
One who possesses faith and diligence and is able to achieve swift supernatural powers is Prince Abhaya; he dwells in the city of Rājagṛha.
One who has severed the roots [of unwholesomeness] and given rise to faith and understanding is King Ajātaśatru, the son of Vaidehī of the kingdom of Magadha; he resides in the city of Rājagṛha.
"In this way, such an upāsaka shall be the foremost among the great assembly.
At that time, the Blessed One again addressed the bhikṣus: "Listen well!
I shall now praise the upāsakas, who, within their hearts of faith, also cultivate their own practice.
These are those who, having first conceived faith, took refuge in the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Saṅgha: namely, the upāsaka Nanda and the upāsaka Nandabala, who dwell in Uruvilvā.
The one who was able to give rise to the initial resolve of faith and understanding regarding the Dharma of the precepts is the mother of the householder Nakula;
she dwells in Vāṇija. The one who constantly practiced giving to the Saṃgha is the female lay disciple Viśākhā; she dwells in Śrāvastī.
The one who, due to her abundant past causes of giving, possesses great merit and virtue, is the mother of the householder Riddhilā; she dwells in the city of Śrāvastī.
The one who prepared medicinal decoctions and gave them to those suffering from illness is the wife of the householder Mahāsena; she dwells in the city of Vārāṇasī.
The one who is able to attend to those who are ill is the householder’s wife Śrīmatī; she resides in the city of Vārāṇasī.
The female lay follower (upāsikā) Śamāvatī, who has long since given rise to faith and constantly practices acts of loving-kindness, resides in the kingdom of Kauśāmbī.
Among the assembly, the one foremost in extensive learning is the upāsaka Kumbhīra; he resides in the kingdom of Kauśāmbī.
She who is well able to expound the sublime Dharma and possesses great eloquence is the daughter of King Subāhu; she resides in the city of Śrāvastī.
She who has long since developed faith and is able to possess great wisdom is the Princess Kuntī; she dwells in Rājagṛha.
She who is foremost in beauty and grace among all forms is the Princess Sujātā; she dwells in Rājagṛha.
The one who is capable of generating faith and understanding, whose mind is well-disposed toward the arousal of the bodhicitta, is the wife of the householder Maitra;
she dwells in Rājagṛha. The one who dwells in the world with many sons is the wife of the householder Jīvaka; she dwells in Rājagṛha.
She who is constantly able to practice and maintain virtue with great diligence is the wife of the householder Śreṣṭhin Suruṇa; she dwells in the city of Campā.
She who is always able to provide dwellings for the Saṃgha is the daughter of the householder Dhanika; she dwells in the Bamboo Grove.
One who has long since developed faith and possesses a profound understanding of meditative concentration is the upāsaka Kāḷa, who dwells within the Bamboo Grove.
Such an upāsaka is the foremost among the great assembly.

At that time, the great assembly of bhikṣus, as well as the devas, humans, asuras, and others, having heard what the Buddha had spoken, were all greatly rejoiced; they believed, accepted, and practiced it accordingly.
The Sūtra on the Virtues of an Arhat Spoken by the Buddha
